segments: And the seventh, Euedoranchos {OCR?};
and the eighth, Amempsinos {OCR?};
and the ninth, Otiartes;
and the tenth, Xisuthros his son,
he in whose days the Deluge occurred.
All these are Chaldeans, that is, ancient Syrians,
according to the tradition of the early chroniclers.
And because the majority of the chroniclers were Greeks,
they changed the Chaldean names into their own dialect,
and did not pronounce them as they were in Chaldean.
For lo, even the name of Noah,
which is a plain Syrian name,
and derived from 'rest' (nawḥā),
they call 'Noachos'.
And not only the ancients,
but even those in our own days are accustomed to altering words,
calling Jacob, which comes from 'heel' (ʿeqbā), 'Iakobos',
and Bar Sawma, 'Barsumos',
and many other things.
[Paragraph] Enoch his son.
At the age of one hundred and sixty-five years he begot Methuselah.
And having pleased God for three hundred years,
he was translated to where God willed,
which is said to be Paradise,
the place where Adam had previously
broken the commandment.
And this Enoch was the first of all men to reveal books and writing.
The ancient Greeks say
that Enoch is Hermes Trismegistus.
And he taught men the building of cities,
and established wondrous laws.
Now in his days one hundred and eighty cities were built,
of which the smallest was Edessa.
And he discovered the knowledge of the constellations and the courses of the stars.
And he enjoined upon men that they should serve God,
and also that they should fast and pray,
and give alms, vows, and tithes.
And he rejected abominable foods and drunkenness; and he also instituted feasts for the entrance of the sun into each sign of the zodiac,
and for the new moon,
and for every star when it enters its house or its culmination.
And he commanded that they offer oblations of perfumes, sacrifices, wine, and every firstfruit.
And they say that from Agathodaemon he received this teaching.
And they say that Agathodaemon is Seth, the son of Adam,
that is to say, the great-grandfather of Enoch.
And they say further
that Asclepiades {OCR? Asclepius}, the wise king, was the disciple of Hermes,
that is, of Enoch.
And when God translated him, he inherited {OCR?} ... the law,
priest,
and philosopher {OCR?}.
